page.name: E-commerce & retail
page.metaDescription: Order confirmations, shipping updates, delivery windows and cart recovery — over the SMS, email and WhatsApp accounts your store already pays for.
page.lede: A storefront runs on the messages customers actually read: the confirmation, the dispatch note, the delivery window, the code after a failed payment. Send all of them over the SMS, email and WhatsApp accounts your store already pays for.

sections.h: The messages your store sends every day
p: Retail traffic divides cleanly into transactional and promotional, and the two have different rules, different send times and very different consequences when they go wrong. The platform treats them as separate message types so the rules never bleed into each other.
bullets: Order confirmation — immediate, must never be throttled away
Dispatch and shipping updates — tied to a fulfillment event
Promotional drops — the only category that should carry suppression rules

sections.h: What the platform takes off your plate
p: Your store keeps its provider accounts; the platform connects to them and takes over the parts a single account cannot do well. Routing and automatic failover, pacing to the real quota your provider grants each number, segment accounting are implemented on the SMS channel, while normalized delivery receipts and opt-out suppression apply across the channels you connect.
bullets: Route SMS across more than one provider account, with failover when one stops accepting traffic
Pace sends to the limit the provider actually applies, per sender number
Normalize delivery receipts from each provider into one status a webhook can read
Apply opt-out suppression to promotional traffic only

p: Consent capture, the wording of your messages, the links and codes inside them, and the records you keep for each customer remain the store’s responsibility. The platform does not decide who may be messaged, and it does not file or guarantee any registration on your behalf.

faq.q: Can the same message go out over email and SMS?
faq.a: The platform connects to the provider accounts you already hold on each channel, so the same event can be carried on whichever channels you have connected. The channels are configured separately, and the delivery guarantees are not identical between them — automatic failover and per-number pacing are SMS-only, while receipts are normalized wherever the provider reports them back.

faq.q: Do you take a cut of what I spend with my provider?
faq.a: No. You keep your own provider contract and pay them directly. The platform is a layer above those accounts, not a reseller of message credits.

faq.q: What happens to a confirmation if my provider goes down?
faq.a: On the SMS channel, traffic can be routed to another connected account instead of failing outright. That changes which provider carries the message; it does not guarantee that the destination carrier will accept it.
